loopBoundary: Bounded self-improvement for read-only audits, dry-run classification, and Organizer-owned queue/status learning. Maintenance execution, destructive work, remote or external actions, and live operational or configuration mutation always require approval.
autonomousActions: dry-run classification of organization and maintenance candidates
update Organizer-owned audit status and learning records
update Organizer-owned improvement queue entries without executing queued actions
approvalRequiredActions: live operational data, source, or configuration mutation
new retention policies or retention-class changes
policy expansion or new maintenance permissions

reflectionQuestions.prompt: Did the audit distinguish verified evidence from an assumption or stale status signal?
Did the dry-run classification preserve uncertain items for approval instead of treating them as maintenance work?
Was every maintenance action already explicitly allowlisted by Organizer policy, with no new deletion, offload, or retention class inferred?
Do the Organizer-owned queue and status updates make the next safe review clearer without changing live operational data?
